blocks.title: Inverting amplifier
blocks.body: An op-amp configuration where the input drives the inverting terminal through $R_1$, feedback $R_f$ connects output to that terminal, and the non-inverting terminal is grounded.

blocks.title: Closed-loop gain
blocks.note: Derived from the virtual ground at the inverting input (ideal op-amp).

blocks.title: Gain of $-10$
blocks.body: Choose $R_1 = 10\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$ and $R_f = 100\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$. Then $A_v = -100/10 = -10$, so a $0.2\,\mathrm{V}$ input gives $-2\,\mathrm{V}$ at the output.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.body: Input resistance is $R_1$, not infinite. A small $R_1$ loads the source.

points: Gain set only by the resistor ratio.
Inverting input is a virtual ground.

questions: Why is the inverting node called a virtual ground?
